kind: assumed inputs for a synthetic model; nothing in this file is measured in the Demerzel repository

error_model.error: error_i = bias + sigma * (sqrt(rho) * C + sqrt(1 - rho) * I_i)

parts.bias: the same number for every forecaster on every occasion
parts.C: the common part: one draw per occasion, shared by every forecaster
parts.I_i: the individual part: one draw per occasion and per forecaster

error_model.draw: (random.Random(seed).random() - 0.5) * sqrt(12): uniform between -sqrt(3) and sqrt(3), mean 0, variance 1; C and every I_i are drawn independently
error_model.consequences: each error has mean bias and variance sigma^2; two errors have correlation rho
error_model.note: A textbook model chosen because every quantity in the lesson has a closed form for it. It is not a model of the project's agents, whose errors nobody has measured. Here 'outcome' stands for the best forecast possible: these errors leave out the part of the outcome nobody could foresee, which yes_no_outcome puts back.

simulation.draw_order: per occasion: C, then I_1 to I_14; the same draws serve every rho and every k (the average of the first k forecasters)

direct_check.note: The first occasions are generated again; each error is built on its own and the errors are averaged one by one. The sums of the fast path at that occasion must agree.

hypothesis_thresholds.note: Written at 2026-10-14T02:11:34Z, before analyze.py existed, and copied unchanged into the research cycle's hypothesis.

exact_enumeration.note: C and every I_i are +1 or -1 with probability 1/2 each (mean 0, variance 1). Every sign pattern is listed and weighted exactly, in fractions.

hand_case.note: Worked by hand in the README: sqrt(0.36) = 0.6 and sqrt(0.64) = 0.8 are exact.

newcomer.note: Thirteen forecasters on one model reading one context, then a fourteenth of four kinds. The split of the shared variance between context and model is invented.
newcomer.error: error_i = sqrt(context_share) * X_context(i) + sqrt(model_share) * Y_model(i) + sqrt(1 - context_share - model_share) * I_i, with sigma = 1 and no bias
newcomer.draw_order: per occasion: X for the panel's context, X for another context, Y for the panel's model, Y for another model, then I_1 to I_14

agreement_of_two.note: A reading that the policy does not state: its confidence settings are taken as probabilities of being right on a yes/no question. Two judges are each right with probability p; rho is the correlation between 'judge 1 is right' and 'judge 2 is right'. On a yes/no question two wrong answers coincide.
agreement_of_two.accuracy_from: the number of single_model in observed-input.json
agreement_of_two.agreement_value_from: the number of two_model_agreement in observed-input.json
agreement_of_two.disagreement_value_from: the number of two_model_disagreement in observed-input.json

scored_log.note: What a log of scored forecasts could tell about rho if the errors left out the part of the outcome nobody could foresee (yes_no_outcome puts it back). One log = a number of occasions, each with the errors of every agent. Estimate: 1 - (k / (k - 1)) * mean spread / mean squared error of one agent.
scored_log.agents_from: the number of personas of the panel in observed-input.json
scored_log.percentile_rule: nearest rank: the value at position ceil(q / 100 * logs) of the sorted estimates
scored_log.draw_order: per log and per occasion: C, then one I per agent; a log of 20 occasions is the first 20 of the 100

yes_no_outcome.note: Logs scored against a yes/no outcome, which puts back the part of the outcome nobody could foresee. On each pull request the true probability p is uniform between the two bounds and the outcome is 1 with probability p. A persona forecasts p + s * (sqrt(rho) * C + sqrt(1 - rho) * I_i); the outsider forecasts p + s * I_o and shares nothing with the panel but the outcome. Every part is +1 or -1 with probability 1/2 (mean 0, variance 1), so every forecast stays between 0 and 1 and the closed forms need no clipping. Error = forecast - outcome.
yes_no_outcome.personas_from: the number of personas of the panel in observed-input.json
yes_no_outcome.draw_order: per log and per pull request: p, the outcome draw, C, I_1 to I_k, I_o; the same draws serve both rhos; a log of 20 pull requests is the first 20 of the 500
yes_no_outcome.estimate_from_the_spread: 1 - (k / (k - 1)) * mean spread / mean variance of one persona's errors (each persona's mean error subtracted)
yes_no_outcome.estimate_against_the_outsider: (mean covariance of two personas' errors - mean covariance of a persona's and the outsider's errors) / (mean variance of a persona's errors - mean covariance of a persona's and the outsider's errors); sample covariances with n - 1

worked_examples.note: Inputs of the lesson's exercises that are not already listed above.

transfer_task.note: Hypothetical estimating team for the learner task. Not Streeling data and not a forecast.
